status: accepted structural partial results; exact target unresolved

independent_structural_checks.method: 3D integer face normals and quarter-turn rotation matrices; independently authored, with no producer verification module imported.

connectivity_obstruction.remaining_graph: two 10-cycles joined by their middle bridge

negative_generated_board_probes.method: Corner-rooted Hamiltonian paths generated by fixed-root backbite moves and labeled by actual die rolls, with actual endpoint orientations used for propagation.
negative_generated_board_probes.limitation: Generated boards may repeat. No proof of a stronger theorem, no exhaustive arbitrary-board test and no attained singleton/domino witness.

prior_source_figure4_replay.source: Marzio De Biasi, Rolling a Cube can be Tricky, May 2012 Version 0.03, Figure 4
prior_source_figure4_replay.initial_state_check: Exactly one initial state in the source-net chirality succeeds on each drawn cycle; none from the other chirality succeeds on those particular cycles. No claim about all other routes on the board.
prior_source_figure4_replay.dash_annotations: All 270 dashes in each drawing are opposite the reference-face direction defined by the manuscript. Reversing them repairs the annotations without changing the labels or cycle edges.
prior_source_figure4_replay.novelty_status: Verification of a known 2012 construction; not a new nonuniqueness result.

prior_source_propagation_regression.instance_transformation: Global label swap 3 and 4, applied to all labels and orientations, transfers the source-net chirality to the reference chirality of this edition.
prior_source_propagation_regression.claim: Existing source examples corroborate propagation and show that pinned orientations do not imply a unique traversal.

interpretation: All finite checks corroborate the complete proofs. They neither classify arbitrary fully labeled rectangles nor establish worldwide novelty. No operational streams or their hashes are reproduced.
